content.text:
All 24 tests still pass.

Refactor Phase Complete

**Naming evaluation (done first)**
- `roundPremiumInMHPCOsFavor` — kept. Already scoped to premium specifically, which leaves room for the payout counterpart the next test pair will demand.
- `quotePremium`, `applyPolicyModifiers`, `runQuoteStep`, `formsABlock` — all kept; each already names exactly what it does.
- `groupByType` → **renamed to `alikeGroups`**. The domain word in the spec and tests is "alike" ("block of 3 alike", "no block: different types"). `groupByType` described the mechanism; `alikeGroups` describes the domain concept, and it now matches its only consumer, `alikeGroupBasePremium`.
- `alikeGroupBasePremium(items)` → parameter renamed to `alikeItems`. The old name implied any item list; the function is only correct for a same-type group.

**Rule 3 / Rule 4 — grouping implementation**

The old `groupByType` built a `Set` of types, then re-scanned the whole array with `filter` once per distinct type — traversing `items` once per type on top of the two `map`s.

APP mass: **32 → 26 (Δ -6)**

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Constants | 0 | 0 |
| Bindings | 5 | 4 (`items`, `groupsByType`, `item`, ×2 uses) |
| Invocations | 6 (=12) | 5 (=10) |
| Loops | 3 (=15) | 2 (=10) — one `for`, one spread |
| Assignments | 0 | 1 (=6) — the `Map.set` |

Mass fell despite introducing an assignment, because two of three traversals collapsed into one. Note this is the honest trade: the `Map` accumulation costs a mutation (mass 6) but removes the quadratic re-filter. Rule 2 is unharmed — arguably helped, since "walk the items, drop each into its type's bucket" is a more direct statement of the intent than "find the distinct types, then re-scan for each."

**Rule 1** — all 24 tests green before and after.

**Note for the next Red phase:** `roundPremiumInMHPCOsFavor` is currently applied only in `quotePremium`, and it is `Math.ceil`. The upcoming payout-rounds-down test will want a sibling (`Math.floor`); the two together may then justify a small shared abstraction, but I deliberately did not build it now — there is no payout path yet, and speculating one would violate Rule 4.
